findings.title: Async legacy writes derive their context from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes
findings.body: In Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection, the goroutine that writes to legacy storage calls `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` using the incoming request `ctx`. In an HTTP/gRPC handler, that context is cancelled as soon as the handler returns — which is exactly when the goroutine starts doing its legacy write. The legacy write will therefore almost always be aborted immediately with context.Canceled, so the "write to legacy as a safe measure" silently never happens. The async write should be derived from a background/detached context (preserving trace/identity values as needed) with its own timeout.

findings.title: Storage Create failure recorded as legacy-duration metric
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails in Mode 3 Create, the error path calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, ...)` with `startStorage` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`. The same mistake exists in Update's error path (line 129). This mislabels unified-storage write failures as legacy-storage failures in the dual-writer metrics, which will mislead operators monitoring the migration.

findings.title: Async legacy DeleteCollection records storage-duration metric
findings.body: In the async legacy branch of DeleteCollection, the legacy call's result is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`, and uses `startLegacy` as the start time. Legacy delete-collection latencies/failures will be attributed to unified storage in the metrics.

findings.title: Delete records storage metric with object name as the kind label
findings.body: On successful storage delete, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object `name` where every other call passes `options.Kind`. The resource/kind label on the metric will contain object names, exploding label cardinality and making the per-kind dashboards useless.

findings.title: Delete installs the wrong logger into the context
findings.body: Delete builds an enriched `log` with name/kind/method values, but then calls `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` — the base logger without those values — so downstream log lines from the delete path lose the contextual fields, unlike all other methods which pass `log`.

findings.title: objInfo is invoked twice for updates; the updateWrapper caching was removed
findings.body: The previous implementation resolved the updated object once via `objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old)` and wrapped it in `updateWrapper` so legacy storage reused the same resolved object. The new code passes the original `objInfo` to both `d.Storage.Update` and, asynchronously, `d.Legacy.Update`, so `UpdatedObject` will be invoked twice — concurrently with the request handler returning. Many UpdatedObjectInfo implementations (e.g., the default one reading the request body) are single-use or not safe to invoke after the request completes, so the legacy update may fail or read inconsistent data.

findings.title: Mode 3 integration tests read from legacy API immediately after async legacy writes
findings.body: The mode 3 subtests reuse doPlaylistTests, which asserts that objects created/updated/deleted via k8s are immediately visible through the legacy /api/playlists endpoints (e.g., getFromBothAPIs, the legacy search listing). In mode 3 the legacy write happens asynchronously in a goroutine, so there is no happens-before guarantee between the k8s write returning and the legacy write landing. These assertions will be flaky under load; the test should poll/retry the legacy read or mode 3 should be excluded from the cross-API consistency assertions.
